exceptions.reason: The repository intentionally permits authorized maintainers and administrators to facilitate a merge after required checks and review-thread resolution, does not require a code-owner or last-pusher approval, and GitHub cannot count an author's documented maintainer review as a formal approval.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove only after an explicit operator governance decision replaces maintainer/admin facilitation and the replacement remains practical for maintainer-authored changes.

exceptions.target: OpenSSF Scorecard PinnedDependenciesID #200 and re-fingerprinted duplicate #221 for npm install --package-lock-only
exceptions.reason: The command installs no named or ad hoc package: it deterministically refreshes each committed infrastructure package-lock from that directory's committed package.json after first-party version synchronization, with lifecycle scripts disabled. Scorecard interprets the lockfile operation as an unpinned package invocation even though dependency resolution is committed and subsequently audited.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove when the release-sync design no longer regenerates infrastructure locks or OpenSSF Scorecard correctly distinguishes lockfile-only refreshes from unpinned package installation.

exceptions.target: TypeScript 6 compatibility API used by ts-jest, ts-node, tsdown, and other compiler-API consumers
exceptions.reason: TypeScript 7.0.2 is the authoritative native CLI compiler but deliberately ships without a stable JavaScript API. The official @typescript/typescript6 compatibility package therefore supplies a peer-compatible API to ts-jest, ts-node, tsdown, and related tools while every direct tsc build and workspace typecheck runs TypeScript 7. This uses the TypeScript team's supported side-by-side layout and no peer override.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove after TypeScript exposes a stable native API, every compiler-API consumer supports it without an override, and the full build, typecheck, declaration, packed-consumer, Jest, conformance, browser/mobile, and infrastructure matrix passes without @typescript/typescript6.

exceptions.target: OpenSSF Scorecard BinaryArtifactsID #196 and #197 for @bsv/verifast WASM
exceptions.reason: The two checked-in WASM modules are required runtime artifacts for browser, worker, ESM, CommonJS, and classic-script consumers. Their pinned BDK source, reproducible build, SHA-256 values, generated-file ownership, ABI tests, package-consumer tests, and bundle budget are enforced; removing them would break zero-install and browser package consumers.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove only when all supported package consumers can obtain the verified WASM reproducibly without install-time network access, lifecycle scripts, mutable build inputs, or a larger supply-chain risk.

exceptions.target: pnpm-workspace.yaml and four standalone Jest service manifests overriding brace-expansion <=5.0.7
exceptions.reason: Jest 30.4.2 still constrains reporting and coverage paths to minimatch releases that require older brace-expansion ranges. GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg required 5.0.8, and the follow-up GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 requires 5.0.9, so the governed substitution selects the current patched release.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove after the supported Jest dependency graph natively resolves brace-expansion 5.0.9 or newer across every coverage and reporting path.

exceptions.target: All seven standalone service manifests and the cloud-bucket notifier override transitive gaxios 6.x/7.1.3 with 7.3.0
exceptions.reason: The 2026-08-30 removal rehearsal regenerated every standalone service lock without the gaxios override. The natural Google client and OpenTelemetry graphs still select gaxios 6.7.1 or 7.1.3 rather than the governed 7.3.0 line. Retaining 7.3.0 removes the obsolete rimraf/glob/minimatch path associated with high-severity GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg without changing a service's direct API; frozen locks, service tests, and hosted image builds verify compatibility.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove service by service when its complete supported Google and OpenTelemetry graph natively resolves gaxios 7.3.0 or newer and frozen audit, build, test, and Linux image checks remain green without the substitution.

exceptions.target: Message Box, UHRP cloud-bucket, and its notifier manifests override transitive uuid releases below 11.1.1
exceptions.reason: The 2026-08-30 removal rehearsal regenerated the Message Box, UHRP cloud-bucket, and notifier locks without the uuid override. Their natural teeny-request and Google client closures still resolve uuid 9.0.1, which npm audit identifies under GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq, instead of the reviewed 11.1.1 line. The override remains limited to those three manifests.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove from each remaining service when its supported cloud client closure natively resolves uuid 11.1.1 or newer and frozen audit, build, test, and Linux image checks remain green without the substitution.

exceptions.reason: The workspace uses Stryker 9.6.1, and the current Stryker 10.0.0 release still depends on typed-rest-client ~2.3.0. typed-rest-client 2.3.1 pins vulnerable qs 6.15.1 exactly. GHSA-q8mj-m7cp-5q26 is fixed in qs 6.15.2 and later, so a parent-scoped substitution to 6.15.3 remains the narrowest durable remediation. The previous lock-only selection was lost when an unrelated dependency change regenerated the graph.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove when Stryker no longer depends on typed-rest-client 2.3.1 or a supported typed-rest-client release natively depends on qs 6.15.2 or newer, then regenerate the lock and rerun the complete mutation campaign.

exceptions.reason: Vite's current PostCSS dependency range can select nanoid releases affected by GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8, whose patched 3.x boundary was raised to 3.3.18 on 2026-08-13. Selecting 3.3.18 is the narrowest compatible remediation and leaves runtime application packages unchanged.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove when the supported Vite and PostCSS dependency graph naturally resolves nanoid 3.3.18 or newer and the frozen audit remains green.

exceptions.target: pnpm-workspace.yaml override for TOML releases below 4.2.0
exceptions.reason: remark-mdx-frontmatter 5.2.0 still constrains its TOML parser dependency to vulnerable 3.x even though it imports only the compatible parse API. GHSA-v5mp-jgw5-2x6j is fixed in 4.1.2, and GHSA-82x6-q7mm-w9cf requires 4.2.0. The workspace already requires Node 24, webpack-cli accepts TOML 4, and the docs validation, tests, and complete production build verify the substitution.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove when remark-mdx-frontmatter or its supported successor natively resolves TOML 4.2.0 or newer and docs validation, tests, production build, and the frozen high-severity audit remain green.

exceptions.target: image-size 1.2.1 pnpm patch and exact audit exclusions for malformed ICNS, HEIF, and JPEG XL records
exceptions.reason: GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr and GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq affect every published image-size release and have no patched version. The committed patch rejects zero or undersized records before parser loops can receive a non-progressing offset; a child-process regression test enforces termination. The audit exclusions cover only those independently remediated advisory IDs.
exceptions.removeWhen: Replace the patch and exact audit exclusions when Metro supports an image-size release that fixes both advisories, then rerun the frozen audit and mobile platform contract.

exceptions.reason: The latest openapi-typescript release still depends on Redocly 1.x ranges that resolve vulnerable js-yaml and minimatch paths, so the isolated codegen lock substitutes compatible patched releases and verifies the generated output byte-for-byte.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove when a supported openapi-typescript release natively resolves non-vulnerable js-yaml, minimatch, and brace-expansion versions, then regenerate and compare every committed output.

exceptions.target: 211 individually reasoned conformance cases across 19 governed vector files
exceptions.reason: Every current non-run vector has a stable ID and inherited or local reason, and every affected file has an exact count, classification, owner, review date, and removal condition. The remaining gaps require stateful/funded/overlay fixtures, upstream parity decisions, or runner work before enforcement can require zero skips.
exceptions.removeWhen: Every conformance skip is implemented or documented as deliberately unsupported with a permanent compatibility decision.

exceptions.target: 6 governed direct skips in required package tests
exceptions.reason: Manual, live, and resource suites are now classified outside deterministic PR discovery. Six required-suite gaps remain individually registered with owner, reason, review date, and removal condition; CI rejects new anonymous skips, stale registrations, and empty test bodies.
exceptions.removeWhen: All six required-suite gaps are enabled, moved to a correctly governed non-PR suite, or removed with evidence that the scenario is obsolete.

exceptions.target: sonar-project.properties and .sonarcloud.properties broad test and generated-file exclusions
exceptions.reason: Legacy Sonar configuration excludes tests broadly and suppresses duplication findings while generated and third-party artifacts are mixed into repository paths; project administration cannot be changed during the current wave.
exceptions.removeWhen: The Sonar backlog wave proves precise source, test, generated, vendored, and coverage boundaries and removes broad exclusions without hiding real findings.

exceptions.target: typescript:S6564 on documented primitive aliases in SDK Wallet.interfaces.ts, remittance/types.ts, and wallet/validationHelpers.ts
exceptions.reason: These aliases are the named BRC-100 and remittance wire vocabulary. Their exported names and JSDoc constraints carry defaults, units, ranges, encodings, and generated-documentation anchors that a bare boolean, number, or string cannot express. Removing them would degrade a stable public declaration and documentation contract without changing runtime or TypeScript assignability.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove when the analyzer distinguishes documented public protocol aliases, or when an SDK major version can adopt a compatibility-preserving nominal representation with generated documentation and packed-consumer proof.

exceptions.target: typescript:S101 on protocol-defined WERR_* error classes
exceptions.reason: The WERR_* identifiers are the stable BRC-100 wallet error vocabulary used in declarations, instanceof checks, serialized error names, HTTP mappings, tests, documentation, and downstream integrations. Renaming the classes would change a public compatibility contract solely to satisfy a generic class-name style rule.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove when the analyzer supports a naming convention exception for protocol-defined public identifiers, or during a coordinated major-version migration that preserves serialized names, declarations, instanceof behavior, HTTP mappings, documentation, and downstream compatibility.

exceptions.reason: Curve construction intentionally returns and initializes the module singleton so repeated new Curve() calls across cryptographic operations share the expensive secp256k1 parameters and precomputation tables. Removing the constructor return or its assignment would change established identity and performance semantics throughout the SDK.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove after a benchmarked major-version design replaces new Curve() singleton semantics with an explicit factory or immutable shared constants and the complete cryptographic, transaction, browser, packed-consumer, and performance suites prove parity.

exceptions.reason: The large switch is the auditable one-to-one dispatch table for Bitcoin Script opcodes. Replacing the exhaustive switch with indirect dynamic dispatch would make opcode coverage and fallthrough behavior harder to review while adding risk to consensus-critical code.
exceptions.removeWhen: Remove when the analyzer exempts exhaustive protocol dispatch or a separately reviewed generated opcode table improves auditability and passes every script vector, differential, mutation, fuzz, transaction, browser, and packed-consumer check.
